newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica-EU finalise multi-billion rand aid package.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica-EU finalise multi-billion rand aid package.

text.p: South Africa and the European Commission on Tuesday finalised a multi-billion rand indicative programme to provide grants and soft loans for development projects between 1997 and 1999.
Under the European Programme for Reconstruction and Development, the EU has already committed about 1.8 billion rand in grants to reconstruction and development in South Africa since 1994.
The two have now finalised a general framework for co-operation over the next three years, during which a further two billion rand will be made available to South Africa.
The agreement was signed by Deputy Finance Minister Gild Marcus and European Commission director general for development Philippe Soubestre.
Marcus said that the framework would ensure that the funds were effectively used and targeted within a clear framework of addressing poverty.
"It does provide us with a focus on education, health care and infrastructure, which is where the needs of South Africans are."
In addition, the two parties also signed a memorandum of understanding with the European Investment Bank (EIB) for a two billion rand soft loan facility.

This brings the total amount that the EIB has made available to South Africa for the period 1995 to 1999 to 3.8 billion rand. The loans will be used to finance productive investments and infrastructral projects.
